### ⚑ Section A · Q3. · a. — 2 marks

> Importance of water in our diet.

- **Answer: Water is an important part of our diet. It helps in digesting food, keeps our skin and body healthy, and removes waste from the body through urine, sweat and faeces. Water-rich fruits like watermelon and cucumber also help keep water in the body.**
- Answer points:
  - Water helps digest food / keeps skin and body healthy (1 mark)
  - Water removes waste from the body (urine, sweat, faeces); drink enough water / eat water-rich fruits (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Two correct points about why water is needed (digestion, healthy skin/body, removing waste, keeping the body cool or hydrated).
  - partial (1 mark): One correct point.
  - none (0 marks): No correct point.
- Model answer: Water helps us digest food and keeps our skin and body healthy. It removes waste from our body through urine and sweat, so we should drink enough water every day.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.12 l.8

### ⚑ Section A · Q3. · b. — 2 marks

> Balanced food

- **Answer: Balanced food has food from all three food groups in the right quantities: protective foods (fruits and vegetables) the most, then body-building foods, and some energy-giving foods. It keeps us healthy, active and happy.**
- Answer points:
  - Contains all three food groups (energy-giving, body-building, protective) in the right amounts (1 mark)
  - Keeps us healthy, active and happy / gives everything the body needs (examples welcome) (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Says balanced food has all the food groups in the right amounts AND why it is good for us.
  - partial (1 mark): Only one of these, or a list of healthy foods without the idea of all food groups.
  - none (0 marks): Nothing correct.
- Model answer: Balanced food has energy-giving, body-building and protective foods in the right amounts, with more fruits and vegetables. It keeps us healthy, active and happy.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.11 l.25

### ⚑ Section B · Q4. · a. — 1 mark

> What did Surabhi’s grandmother use to eat to during summers and winters?

- **Answer: She used to eat jau (barley) roti during summers and jowar and bajra roti in winters.**
- Also accept: jau roti in summers, jowar and bajra roti in winters · barley roti in summer, jowar and bajra roti in winter · jowar bajra roti in winter and jau roti in summer
- Rubric:
  - full (1 mark): Summers: jau (barley) roti AND winters: jowar and/or bajra roti (millet rotis).
  - partial (0.5 marks): Only one season correct, or just "millet rotis" without the seasons.
  - none (0 marks): No correct food.
- Model answer: In summers she ate jau roti, and in winters she ate jowar and bajra roti.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.6 l.35
- Teacher note: Printed as "use to eat to" (stray "to"; means "used to eat") and "Surabhi" (the textbook spells it "Surbhi"). Kept as printed. Answers that spell the name either way (Surabhi / Surbhi) are fully correct.

### ⚑ Section B · Q4. · b. — 1 mark

> Why do you think we should avoid eating junk food?

- **Answer: Junk food has high amounts of oil, salt and sugar, so eating it regularly and in large quantities is not healthy for us.**
- Rubric:
  - full (1 mark): A sensible reason: too much oil, salt or sugar; makes us unhealthy, fat or ill; has little nutrition.
  - partial (0.5 marks): A vague reason ("it is bad") with no explanation.
  - none (0 marks): No sensible reason.
- Model answer: Junk food has too much oil, salt and sugar, so it is not good for our health.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.10 l.2

### ⚑ Section B · Q4. · c. — 1 mark

> Why do we need to eat different kinds of food items?

- **Answer: No single food contains all the nutrients our body needs, so we must eat a variety of foods to stay healthy, energetic and strong.**
- Rubric:
  - full (1 mark): Says no single food has all the nutrients / we need energy, body-building and protection, so we eat many kinds of food.
  - partial (0.5 marks): Says only "to stay healthy" without the reason.
  - none (0 marks): No sensible reason.
- Model answer: No single food has all the nutrients our body needs, so we eat different foods to stay healthy and strong.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.8 l.1

### ⚑ Section B · Q4. · d. — 1 mark

> How is solar cooker useful to us?

- **Answer: A solar cooker cooks food using sunlight instead of gas or electricity, and it does not pollute the environment with smoke or ash.**
- Rubric:
  - full (1 mark): Cooks food with sunlight (saves gas/fuel/electricity) AND/OR causes no smoke or pollution.
  - partial (0.5 marks): Says only "it cooks food" without mentioning sunlight or no pollution.
  - none (0 marks): No sensible answer.
- Model answer: It cooks food with sunlight, so it saves gas and does not make smoke or ash.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.14 l.19

### ⚑ Section B · Q4. · e. — 1 mark

> Who is a ‘Chef’?

- **Answer: A chef is a professional cook who is skilled in all aspects of food preparation. In French, ‘chef’ means the head of the kitchen.**

### ⚑ Section C · Q9. — 3 marks

> Match the following.

- Pairs:
  - a. Boiling → rice
  - b. Steaming → idiyappam
  - c. Frying → puri
  - d. Roasting → popcorn
  - e. Grilling → chicken
  - f. Baking → cakes
- **Answer: a. Boiling – rice; b. Steaming – idiyappam; c. Frying – puri; d. Roasting – popcorn; e. Grilling – chicken; f. Baking – cakes.**
- Answer points:
  - Boiling – rice (0.5 marks)
  - Steaming – idiyappam (0.5 marks)
  - Frying – puri (0.5 marks)
  - Roasting – popcorn (or chicken) (0.5 marks)
  - Grilling – chicken (or popcorn) (0.5 marks)
  - Baking – cakes (0.5 marks)
- Rubric:
  - full (3 marks): All six pairs correct (Roasting/Grilling may be popcorn/chicken either way).
  - partial (1.5 marks): Some pairs correct: ½ mark for each correct pair.
  - none (0 marks): No pair correct.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.13 l.17
- Teacher note: Popcorn and chicken can each be cooked by roasting or grilling, so Roasting – chicken with Grilling – popcorn is also accepted. The printed mark bracket "( 6 x ½ = 3)" has no space before ")"; kept.

#### ⚑ Section B · Q4. · c. — 1 mark

> Why do we need to eat different kinds of food items?

- **Answer: No single food contains all the nutrients our body needs, so we must eat a variety of foods to stay healthy, energetic and strong.**
- Rubric:
  - full (1 mark): Says no single food has all the nutrients / we need energy, body-building and protection, so we eat many kinds of food.
  - partial (0.5 marks): Says only "to stay healthy" without the reason.
  - none (0 marks): No sensible reason.
- Model answer: No single food has all the nutrients our body needs, so we eat different foods to stay healthy and strong.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.8 l.1

#### ⚑ Section B · Q4. · d. — 1 mark

> How is solar cooker useful to us?

- **Answer: A solar cooker cooks food using sunlight instead of gas or electricity, and it does not pollute the environment with smoke or ash.**
- Rubric:
  - full (1 mark): Cooks food with sunlight (saves gas/fuel/electricity) AND/OR causes no smoke or pollution.
  - partial (0.5 marks): Says only "it cooks food" without mentioning sunlight or no pollution.
  - none (0 marks): No sensible answer.
- Model answer: It cooks food with sunlight, so it saves gas and does not make smoke or ash.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.14 l.19

#### ⚑ Section B · Q4. · e. — 1 mark

> Who is a ‘Chef’?

- **Answer: A chef is a professional cook who is skilled in all aspects of food preparation. In French, ‘chef’ means the head of the kitchen.**
- Rubric:
  - full (1 mark): A professional / trained / skilled cook, or the head of a kitchen.
  - partial (0.5 marks): Says only "a person who cooks" (any cook at home).
  - none (0 marks): No sensible answer.
- Model answer: A chef is a professional cook who is skilled in preparing food.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.14 l.5

**Q5. — Write the difference between. ( 2 x 1 = 2 )**

#### ⚑ Section B · Q5. — 1 mark

> Protective Foods

- **Answer: Protective foods help us fight against diseases and protect us from them. Examples: fruits and vegetables like carrot, orange, papaya, spinach, guava, amla, tomato.**
- Rubric:
  - full (1 mark): Says they protect us from / help us fight diseases (an example is welcome).
  - partial (0.5 marks): Gives only examples of protective foods, with no description.
  - none (0 marks): Wrong or no description.
- Model answer: They protect us from diseases, e.g. carrot, orange, spinach.
- Marking guide: 1 mark for the protective-foods column. Accept the job (protect from diseases) with or without examples; examples alone get ½.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.9 l.19
- Teacher note: Printed "( 2 x 1 = 2 )" for a two-column table with one empty row. Read as 1 mark per column (describe each food type). A child who writes the difference as a pair of contrasting sentences also gets full marks.

#### ⚑ Section B · Q5. — 1 mark

> Energy Giving Foods

- **Answer: Energy-giving foods give our body energy to work and play. Examples: rice, wheat, potato, maize, banana, sweet potato, honey, millets, butter, ghee, oil.**
- Rubric:
  - full (1 mark): Says they give us energy (an example is welcome).
  - partial (0.5 marks): Gives only examples of energy-giving foods, with no description.
  - none (0 marks): Wrong or no description.
- Model answer: They give us energy to work and play, e.g. rice, wheat, potato.
- Marking guide: 1 mark for the energy-giving-foods column. Accept the job (give energy) with or without examples; examples alone get ½.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.9 l.1
- Teacher note: Printed "( 2 x 1 = 2 )" for a two-column table with one empty row. Read as 1 mark per column (describe each food type).

**Q7. — Draw any two junk food and also write the names. ( 2 x 1 = 2 )**

#### ⚑ Section B · Q7. · Box 1 — 1 mark

> Draw any two junk food and also write the names.

- **Answer: A recognisable drawing of one junk food with its name, e.g. burger, pizza, chips, soft drink, bread pakoda, noodles, French fries, packaged snacks.**
- Rubric:
  - full (1 mark): A junk food drawn recognisably AND correctly named.
  - partial (0.5 marks): Drawing or name only, or a healthy food drawn.
  - none (0 marks): Nothing drawn or named, or both wrong.
- Model answer: A drawing of a burger, named "Burger".
- Marking guide: Box 1: ½ for a recognisable drawing of a junk food, ½ for writing its correct name. Junk food = food high in oil, salt or sugar (textbook: soft drinks, chips, bread pakoda, burgers, pizza, over-processed packaged food).

#### ⚑ Section B · Q7. · Box 2 — 1 mark

> Draw any two junk food and also write the names.

- **Answer: A recognisable drawing of a second, different junk food with its name, e.g. pizza, chips, soft drink, bread pakoda, noodles, French fries, packaged snacks.**
- Rubric:
  - full (1 mark): A second, different junk food drawn recognisably AND correctly named.
  - partial (0.5 marks): Drawing or name only, a repeat of Box 1, or a healthy food drawn.
  - none (0 marks): Nothing drawn or named, or both wrong.
- Model answer: A drawing of a packet of chips, named "Chips".
- Marking guide: Box 2: ½ for a recognisable drawing of a different junk food from Box 1, ½ for its correct name.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.10 l.5

**Q9. — Match the following. ( 6 x ½ = 3)**

#### ⚑ Section C · Q9. — 3 marks

> Match the following.

- Pairs:
  - a. Boiling → rice
  - b. Steaming → idiyappam
  - c. Frying → puri
  - d. Roasting → popcorn
  - e. Grilling → chicken
  - f. Baking → cakes
- **Answer: a. Boiling – rice; b. Steaming – idiyappam; c. Frying – puri; d. Roasting – popcorn; e. Grilling – chicken; f. Baking – cakes.**
- Answer points:
  - Boiling – rice (0.5 marks)
  - Steaming – idiyappam (0.5 marks)
  - Frying – puri (0.5 marks)
  - Roasting – popcorn (or chicken) (0.5 marks)
  - Grilling – chicken (or popcorn) (0.5 marks)
  - Baking – cakes (0.5 marks)
- Rubric:
  - full (3 marks): All six pairs correct (Roasting/Grilling may be popcorn/chicken either way).
  - partial (1.5 marks): Some pairs correct: ½ mark for each correct pair.
  - none (0 marks): No pair correct.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.13 l.17
- Teacher note: Popcorn and chicken can each be cooked by roasting or grilling, so Roasting – chicken with Grilling – popcorn is also accepted. The printed mark bracket "( 6 x ½ = 3)" has no space before ")"; kept.

  - full (1 mark): The correct state is marked and named.
  - partial (0.5 marks): Marked near the right place but spilling into a neighbouring state, or marked without a name.
